content:
# Grammarly vs QuillBot: Which Writing Helper Wins

These two get compared constantly, but they solve different problems. [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]] is a layer that sits over everything you write and corrects it in place. [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]] is a workbench you paste text into when you want it reworked.

Which one you want depends on whether your problem is "I make mistakes while writing" or "this paragraph needs to be different".

---

## [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]]: Correction Where You Already Write

Grammarly's strength is placement. It works inside the text box you are already using - browser, document editor, email client - and flags grammar, clarity and tone as you type. The generative features now also handle drafting and rewriting in place, so you can ask for a shorter version without leaving the page.

The value is that it is always on. You do not decide to use it; it is simply watching while you write.

**Where it fits:** anyone who writes in many places and wants consistent correction everywhere.
**Trade-off:** it is corrective rather than transformative. It will tighten a sentence, but it will not restructure an argument.

### Why Choose Grammarly?
- Works across browsers, editors and email without switching tools
- Catches grammar, clarity and tone as you type
- Generative rewriting and tone shifts available in place
- Free tier covers the core correction use case

**Add [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]]** if you want one correction layer everywhere you write.

---

## [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]]: A Rewriting Workbench

QuillBot is built around taking text you already have and producing a different version of it. Paraphrasing is the headline feature, supported by grammar checking, summarisation and citation tools. It ships as a web app, a browser extension and a Word add-in.

It is aimed at students and editors - people who routinely need the same material expressed differently, or condensed, or properly attributed.

**Where it fits:** students, editors, anyone reworking existing text.
**Trade-off:** it is a destination, not a layer. You go to it deliberately rather than having it watch your writing.

### Why Choose QuillBot?
- Paraphrasing with adjustable strength rather than a single rewrite
- Summarisation for condensing long material
- Citation tooling aimed at academic work
- Browser extension and Word add-in for where the work happens

**Try [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]]** if your real task is rewriting rather than correcting.

---

## Head-to-Head

| | Grammarly | QuillBot |
|---|---|---|
| Model | Correction layer everywhere | Rewriting workbench |
| Pricing model | Freemium | Freemium |
| Core strength | Grammar, clarity, tone in place | Paraphrase, summarise, cite |
| Best for | Daily writing across many apps | Students and editors |
| Works while you type | Yes | Via extension, limited |

---

## Which One Should You Pick?

**Pick [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]]** if you want fewer errors in everything you write, everywhere, without changing how you work.

**Pick [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]]** if your recurring job is taking existing text and making it different, shorter, or properly cited.

They are not really substitutes. Plenty of people run both: Grammarly catching mistakes as they type, QuillBot open in a tab for the passages that need reworking. If you are choosing one, choose by which of those two jobs you do more often.

---

## FAQ

**Do I need both?**
Only if you both write constantly and routinely rework existing text. Most people have one dominant need.

**Is the free tier enough?**
For Grammarly, the free tier covers core grammar and clarity, which is the main reason to install it. For QuillBot, free works for occasional paraphrasing; heavy use hits limits quickly.

**Which is better for academic writing?**
[[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]], because of the summarisation and citation tooling built for that workflow.
